title: Mutate state in place + rerender from live state to avoid stale closures in vanilla-DOM popups
trigger: A vanilla-DOM popup has async tab callbacks (translation, audio fetch) that mutate state and trigger a rerender. If helpers return a new immutable state object, closures that captured the old state object keep mutating the stale copy, so the rerender shows old data. This is especially sharp when a single toolbar binds to an 'active candidate' that can switch — the callback must read/write the active candidate's slice, not the winner's.
principle: When a vanilla-DOM popup has async callbacks that mutate state and rerender, prefer mutating the live state object in place and reading from it during rerender, instead of returning a new immutable state object. Pair this with getActiveSnapshot/setActiveSnapshot helpers that route reads/writes to the right slice (winner fields or candidateStates Map) based on activeCandidateIndex. This eliminates the 'state = helper(state)' discipline that breaks when an async callback closes over an old state reference. The rerender function reads from the live state, so it always sees the latest data. Trade-off: the state object is no longer immutable, so React-style time-travel debugging won't work — acceptable for vanilla-DOM popups where the state is a single mutable singleton.

cases.context: Popup dictionary redesign: single toolbar binds to active candidate. Translation callback fires async, mutates state, and rerenders. If setActiveSnapshot returns a new state object, the callback's closed-over `state` is stale and the next mutation writes to the old copy.

applyFor: Vanilla-DOM popups with async tab callbacks (translation, audio/image fetch)
Single-toolbar-multiple-candidate patterns where the toolbar binds to an 'active' item
Any vanilla-DOM state singleton where closures + async callbacks coexist
